SoftBank Newsroom article, Tomakomai local engagement (2026-02-18)

records.project: Kobe underground tunnel data centre (Mitsui Fudosan, Kumagai Gumi, Getworks)
records.verbatim: 最大受電容量20メガワット規模のデータセンターとして運用することを目指しています

translation.text: The company aims to operate it as a data centre with a maximum receiving capacity on the order of 20 megawatts.

records.notes: First-party: Mitsui Fudosan news release 2026-10-06. Target capacity, not contracted. Phase 1 scope (containers, service start end-2027) is in the same release.

records.project: Kobe underground tunnel data centre (Mitsui Fudosan, Kumagai Gumi, Getworks)
records.verbatim: 地下水を循環利用する水冷方式を導入するなど、既存資源を最大限に活用することで、環境負荷の低減と高効率な運用を実現します。

translation.text: By introducing a water-cooling system that circulates groundwater, and by making maximum use of existing resources, the company will reduce environmental impact and achieve highly efficient operation.

records.notes: First-party design claim. Groundwater circulation is the stated cooling method; the release does not give a withdrawal or discharge volume, so this is not a water-use figure.

records.project: Kobe underground tunnel data centre (Mitsui Fudosan, Kumagai Gumi, Getworks)
records.verbatim: 初期開発では、2027年末のサービス提供開始を予定しています。

translation.text: For the initial development, the company plans to start service at the end of 2027.

records.notes: First-party schedule claim. Kobe city's lease award (2026-10-06, already in jp_ar_cl_r2) is the government-side record of the same project.

records.verbatim: 北海道内の再生可能エネルギーを100％利用する地産地消型のAIデータセンター

translation.text: an AI data centre that uses 100% renewable energy generated within Hokkaido, consumed locally

records.notes: First-party: SoftBank Newsroom, construction-start release (ceremony 2025-04-15, release 2025-04-21). The 100% figure is the company's own design target; whether it is met in operation is not verified.

records.verbatim: 将来的に国内最大規模の敷地面積70万平方メートル、受電容量が300メガワット超まで拡大

translation.text: Looking ahead, the site is expected to grow to the largest scale in Japan, with a site area of 700,000 square metres and receiving capacity above 300 MW.

records.notes: First-party, future-tense scale claim ('expected to grow'). Phase-1 capacity is not stated in this release, so do not read 300 MW as the current figure.

records.verbatim: 地域経済への波及や雇用の創出、先端産業が集積していくことによる地域の活性化など

translation.text: the spillover into the regional economy, job creation, and revitalisation through the agglomeration of advanced industries

records.notes: First-party company article (interview with SoftBank project staff, published by SoftBank). Company-stated benefit intent, not a job count. Quote is from a staff member, not an executive.

records.verbatim: 近年、AIの普及によりデータセンターで利用する電力や水資源の需要が増加し

translation.text: In recent years, growing use of AI has increased demand for electricity and water resources used by data centres.

records.notes: First-party sustainability statement, issued with the Nature Symbiosis Site certification release (2026-06-30). Acknowledges water demand; gives no site water figure.

records.verbatim: 敷地内の20ha（「自然共生サイト」は13.5ha）を緑地として残し

translation.text: the company will keep 20 ha of the site as green space (13.5 ha of which is certified as a Nature Symbiosis Site)

records.notes: First-party, biodiversity commitment on site. Does not map to a THEMES value cleanly; theme_hint set to engagement as a placeholder for curator review.

records.project: Ishikari bay new port area (Ishikari DC Consortium)
records.verbatim: 「地域の計算資源」かつ「社会インフラ」と位置づけ

translation.text: The consortium positions data centres as 'regional computing resources' and 'social infrastructure'.

records.notes: City of Ishikari news release (2026-07-28) establishing the Ishikari Data Centre Consortium (石狩DCC). Government first-party. Participants listed as planned, not confirmed; Sakura Internet is among them.

records.project: Ishikari bay new port area (Ishikari DC Consortium)
records.verbatim: DC間での人材交流、雇用の創出を推進するほか

translation.text: The consortium will promote engineer training, staff exchange between data centres, and job creation, in addition to building local understanding among residents and local firms.

records.notes: Same city release as r3-JP-9. Consortium plans to promote job creation; no number is given. Prose is the city's, so the quote is government-first-party.

leads.item: Hokkaido Prefecture and SoftBank comprehensive partnership agreement, signed 2025-04-15 at the Hokkaido government office, with new items on industrial revitalisation from the Tomakomai data centre
leads.status: verified in SoftBank release; not yet a Policy record
leads.notes: Source is SoftBank release sbnews/entry/20250421_01 (quotes the agreement). A benefit-agreement candidate for the Policies tab. The agreement text itself is not fetched; its key_terms need the Hokkaido government page before any record is made.

leads.item: MIC/METI 'Watt-Bit Collaboration Public-Private Council' (ワット・ビット連携官民懇談会), first meeting 2025-03-21
leads.status: verified text, probe could not read
leads.notes: Soumu press release (2025-03-18), https://www.soumu.go.jp/menu_news/s-news/01kiban04_02000254.html. Shift-JIS encoded; probe.py decodes UTF-8 only, so its MISS is an encoding limit, not a wrong quote. Needs a probe fix or a curl+decode check before a record. Policy context, not a community benefit.

leads.item: Kitakyushu Wakamatsu data centre consultation council (3-party, announced 2026-10-15 per news)
leads.notes: Still open from round 2. The city PDF 001218667 is image-only and no city press release for 2026-10-15 was found in search. Read city.kitakyushu.lg.jp press listing directly.

leads.item: Mitsui Fudosan: ¥600bn+ cumulative data-centre investment to FY2035 (reported July 2026)
leads.notes: Appears in a trade-press summary of the Kobe release, not in the primary release text pulled here. Do not record until a Mitsui primary is read.

leads.item: AWS Japan cloud infrastructure investment (about JPY 2.26tn, through 2027)
leads.notes: Secondary reports disagree on date (2024 vs 2026) and amount (JPY 2.26tn vs 2.3tn over five years). aboutamazon.jp page was not reachable by search. Verify the primary before any record.

leads.item: Google Inzai (Chiba) data centre first-party page
leads.notes: Search did not return a blog.google/intl/ja-jp post. Opening was 2023-04 per trade press; the official Japanese post would need direct navigation.
No Sakura press release on Ishikari employment found. Sakura is a named Ishikari DCC participant (r3-JP-9/10), so a Sakura primary would be the strongest company record for that consortium.
